newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong judges to keep robes and wigs--official.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong judges to keep robes and wigs--official.

text.p: It's official -- Hong Kong judges can retain gowns and bench wigs as symbols of office.
The British-style judicial system has judges wearing black robes and white wigs in traditional English custom.
There has been speculation over whether this will survive after Hong Kong becomes part of China at midnight next Monday.
But future Chief Justice Andrew Li, who will take over on July 1, decided on Wednesday there would be no change in the practice, the judiciary said in a statement to media.

Noting that the judiciary had decided to keep the attire in a review of the issue two years ago, it said: "The Chief Justice decided to respect that decision and intended to review the matter at an appropriate time in the future."
